title: Dependability Vanguard — 90 Day Collaboration Map
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a cross-functional 90-day collaboration plan (the 'Vanguard') to raise service dependability for high-traffic model endpoints ahead of Q2 launches. It is purposely pragmatic: a set of short workstreams, concrete handoffs, visible metrics, and an escalation fabric so feature teams can keep moving while we harden operational posture.

High-level objective:
- Move three priority services from ‘feature-first’ to ‘dependability-first’ operational posture so they meet latency and availability SLOs under 95th percentile load spikes by the end of the 90-day window.

Scope (in):
- Production model serving endpoints (hosted API and Dedicated), request routing, autoscaling decisions, cache warming, and tracing instrumentation.
- Instrumenting KPI dashboards and two runbooks per service (triage + canary rollback).

Scope (out):
- Model retraining or model quality regressions (handled by Applied ML team separately).
- Long-term infra redesign beyond triage/mitigation patterns.

Target outcomes (measurable):
- SLO targets: 99.9% availability over 1-minute windows and p95 tail latency < 200ms for key low-latency routes (where product constraints allow).
- Reduce incident MTTR by 35% for model-serving incidents tied to routing or autoscale failures.
- Two automated observability checks deployed per service (latency spike detector + cache miss spike detector).

Stakeholders & roles:
- Program lead: Asha Patel (SRE) — program coordination, exec updates, cross-team unblocks.
- Service stewards: Feature team leads (Maya Chen for Search, Diego Romero for Chat, Elliot Brooks for Inference API).
- Infra partner: Nate Huang (Platform Engineering) — autoscale tuning, capacity planning.
- Observability: Priya Srinivasan (Observability) — dashboards, alert tuning, synthetic checks.
- Oncall liaisons: one SRE per service for shadowing and runbook validation.

Workstreams (parallel):
1) Baseline & signal harvest (weeks 0–2)
   - Collect historical traffic shapes and incident postmortems for each service.
   - Define golden queries and synthetic traces to reproduce high-cost paths.
   - Deliverable: short baseline report + initial dashboard.

2) Quick mitigations & guardrails (weeks 2–5)
   - Implement circuit-breaker thresholds and fast failover routes for model variants.
   - Add conservative autoscale guard rails (min/max) per traffic tier.
   - Deploy two lightweight runbooks: immediate triage checklist + rollback checklist.

3) Observability hardening (weeks 3–8)
   - Create latency distribution metrics per model variant and per route.
   - Add sparse sampling of full request traces for tail-latency attribution.
   - Implement synthetic monitoring (5m cadence) with alerting to oncall + pager.

4) Capacity & routing simulations (weeks 5–10)
   - Run traffic replays at 1.5x and 2x expected Q2 peak using staging infrastructure.
   - Validate smart routing fallbacks (e.g., route to quantized variant under capacity pressure).
   - Deliverable: capacity runbook with recommended reserved headroom.

5) Resilience drills & handoffs (weeks 8–12)
   - Tabletop for cross-team incident playthroughs; live canary exercise for routing fallback.
   - Formalize handoff: feature team owns post-drill action list, SRE signs off on runbooks.
   - Deliverable: drill retro + updated runbooks.

Timeline snapshot (by week):
- Week 0 (kickoff): stakeholder alignment, finalize scope, lock metrics.
- Week 1–2: baselines complete; synthetic checks drafted.
- Week 3–5: deploy immediate mitigations; runbook draft validated by oncall.
- Week 6–8: observability rollout; synthetic alerts on fire.
- Week 9–10: capacity simulations; routing fallback validations.
- Week 11–12: resilience drills; signoffs and exec readout.

Decision authority matrix:
- Runbook changes that affect rollback behavior: SRE lead + service steward signoff.
- Any capacity or cost tradeoffs > 25% monthly delta: Platform Eng + Product review.
- Emergency bypass (temp config changes during incident): oncall lead with postmortem within 72 hours.

Success metrics & signals to watch:
- SLOs: rolling 7-day and 30-day windows, p95 latency and availability flashes.
- MTTR measured in minutes; target 35% reduction from baseline.
- Number of false positives from synthetic checks < 10% over a 30-day period.

Risk register (top 6):
- Risk: Instrumentation blindspots for rare long tails. Mitigation: prioritize trace sampling on the longest-tenured code paths and add extra retention for tail traces during experiments.
- Risk: Autoscale policies cause oscillation. Mitigation: conservative step-scaling and warmup delays; canary changes to a single region first.
- Risk: Cross-team bandwidth constraints. Mitigation: timeboxed tasks with clear acceptance criteria and weekly triage to reassign blockers.
- Risk: Cost blowouts from synthetic load tests. Mitigation: cap replay rates, use staging quotas, and pre-approve cost envelope.

Communication cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync on Fridays: status, blockers, decisions.
- Biweekly exec brief: program lead to present headline metrics and major risks.
- Slack channel: #dependability-vanguard — triage in real time; threads for workstream updates.

Runbooks & artifacts to create or update:
- Triage checklist (service-specific) — owner: service steward.
- Canary rollback playbook — owner: Platform Eng.
- Synthetic check definitions + alerting docs — owner: Observability.
- Post-drill retro template and action tracker — owner: Program lead.

Next steps (first 7 days):
- 1) Kickoff meeting with all stakeholders (Asha) — schedule and agenda posted to Slack.
- 2) Each service steward to submit baseline packet: traffic curves, recent incidents, current alerts.
- 3) Observability to share synthetic checklist prototype for rapid feedback.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive but light-touch on implementation details; expect feature teams to propose deviations where product constraints conflict with the general SLO targets.
- Document will be refreshed after the kickoff; please annotate linked artifacts or drop quick comments in the Slack channel.

Appendix (quick references):
- Example SLO snippets: availability window definition, p95 latency calculation method, and error budget cadence.
- Incident postmortem template link: see linked_artifacts.

Prepared by: Asha Patel (SRE)
Revision history: 2026-01-10 initial draft; 2026-02-22 updated owners and timeline after stakeholder workshop.
